sections.html:
Kalispell is the county seat of Flathead County and the largest city in northwest Montana, with 24,558 residents in the 2020 census. It sits at 3,084 feet, about 7 miles north of Flathead Lake. Health care is the biggest employer, led by Logan Health Medical Center, and tourism around Whitefish Mountain Resort adds seasonal work. That mix means buyers range from year-round local workers to people eyeing a second home.

Winters are long, cold and moderately snowy, with snow from late October or early November through March, and summers are hot and dry. A roof carries that snow for five months, and a furnace runs for a long season. Buyers will ask how old both are, so find the dates before you list. Dry summers also put the spotlight on yard and exterior upkeep at showings.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The Flathead County Treasurer collects property tax in two halves. Treasurer's office: 290 A North Main, Kalispell, 406-758-5680.

PaymentDue dateDelinquent after
First halfNovember 30December 1
Second halfMay 31June 1

When a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, you can pay without penalty until 5:00 p.m. the next business day. The treasurer mails bills at least 30 days before November 30. If a bill goes out later than that, the taxpayer gets 30 days from the postmark.

sections.h2: Monthly payment plan for a primary residence
sections.html:
Owners of a primary residence can ask for an alternate schedule of seven monthly payments between November 30 and May 31 under section 15-16-122 of the Montana Code. Applications are due September 30 of the taxing year, so a request in the fall is too late for that year's bill.

If you plan to sell, a plan like this keeps you current while the house is on the market. Whatever is still unpaid is normally settled at closing out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: How Montana values your home and sets the rate
sections.html:
Residential property is valued every two years at 100 percent of market value. For tax year 2025 the rate on a home is 0.76 percent on the first $400,000 of market value, 1.10 percent from $400,000 to $1.5 million and 2.20 percent above that. Your bill depends on where your home's value falls across those bands, plus local levies.

Buyers will often look up the current tax bill on the county's online tax lookup, so pull it up yourself before you set a price.

sections.h2: Short-term rental and accessory unit rules
sections.html:
Rules differ between the city and the surrounding county, and they can matter if your house has been used as a vacation rental. Inside the city, the municipal code has short-term residential rental standards and accessory dwelling unit provisions. Outside the city limits, Flathead County has its own rules.

The county defines a short-term rental as a residential use in a dwelling designed for stays of less than 30 days. In most zoned areas it needs an administrative conditional use permit. Review can take up to a month and a half and includes notice to every owner within 150 feet. Some zones permit short-term rentals outright, some do not allow them, and in unzoned areas Planning and Zoning requires no permit.

A buyer, cash or otherwise, will want to know whether the permit is in place and whether it transfers. Ask the planning office before you list and keep the paperwork together.

sections.h2: What you must tell a buyer in Montana
sections.html:
Montana sellers give a written statement of known problems. It covers:

  • Problems with title or your ability to transfer the property.
  • Issues with water, wells, wastewater or septic systems and utility connections.
  • Structural, roof, foundation, plumbing, electrical or heating problems, and water intrusion.
  • Additions or alterations made without a building permit.
  • Hazardous materials, pests, soil or drainage problems, and any testing for radon, mold, lead-based paint or contaminated soil.

Section 70-20-502 of the Montana Code requires the statement before or with the contract. If it arrives later, the buyer has three days to rescind under section 70-20-504, unless the buyer waived that right. Under section 70-20-503, transfers under a court order, foreclosure sales, and transfers to a spouse, child or parent are exempt.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Kalispell house
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself or sell for cash.

  • Listing with an agent offers the widest reach, but it brings showings, an inspection and a buyer's loan.
  • Selling it yourself saves a commission, and the paperwork and disclosure fall to you.
  • Selling for cash means the buyer takes the house as it is and no lender holds up the closing. The price reflects the work and risk the buyer takes on, so put the written offer next to what you would net after a listing.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or a loan owed
sections.html:
Whichever route you pick, start with paperwork. Ask your lender for a payoff statement, and note any liens, back taxes or HOA dues before you sign anything. Taxes still owed are paid from your sale proceeds at closing, so the title company will want the current figure from the Treasurer.

A short checklist to bring to a first conversation with a buyer or agent:

  • Your latest property tax bill and any payment-plan paperwork.
  • The loan payoff statement.
  • Dates for the roof and furnace.
  • Permits for additions, and the short-term rental permit if one applies.
  • Notes on well, septic or access, for rural lots.

• A vacation or short-term rental whose permit status is unclear.
  • A rural or county property where well, septic or access questions need answers.
  • An inherited house shared among relatives who live in other states.
  • A move for work or family on a fixed date.
  • Back taxes or a loan payment that has fallen behind.

Most of these get easier once the paperwork is gathered, and a cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, which helps when the date is fixed.

faqs.q: When are Flathead County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 30 and the second half is due May 31. Unpaid amounts become delinquent on December 1 and June 1.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Kalispell property tax in monthly installments?
faqs.a: Owners of a primary residence can ask the Flathead County Treasurer for seven monthly payments between November 30 and May 31. Applications are due September 30 of the taxing year.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent my Kalispell house short term?
faqs.a: In most zoned areas of Flathead County an administrative conditional use permit is required. Inside the city, check the municipal code or call the city's Development Services Department.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems with my house in Montana?
faqs.a: Yes. You must disclose adverse material facts you actually know, in writing, before or with the contract. Some transfers, such as those ordered by a court, are exempt.

faqs.q: Can a cash buyer close without an inspection or a loan?
faqs.a: A cash buyer does not need a lender, so there is no loan approval or lender appraisal. Whether the buyer inspects the house is a term of the contract.
